senses.definition: An arthropod (in the Insecta class) characterized by six legs, up to four wings, and a chitinous exoskeleton.
examples: Our shed has several insect infestions, including ants, yellowjackets, and wasps.

quotes.text: Nonetheless, some insect prey take advantage of clutter by hiding in it. Earless ghost swift moths become “invisible” to echolocating bats by forming mating clusters close (less than half a meter) above vegetation and effectively blending into the clutter of echoes that the bat receives from the leaves and stems around them.
quotes.reference: 2013 May-June, William E. Conner, “An Acoustic Arms Race”, in American Scientist, volume 101, number 3, pages 206–7:

senses.definition: (archaic or loosely) Any small arthropod similar to an insect, including spiders, centipedes, millipedes, etc.
examples: The swamp is swarming with every sort of insect.
The manager’s assistant was the worst sort of insect.
